A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same 39-page work with complete main text, references, figures, tables and Appendices A.1–A.9. Pages 2–39 match in extracted text and rendered appearance; the first-page differences are fully identifiable.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark experiments, ablations and citation analyses, plus a user study involving 20 participants and 71 reports (Section 4 and Appendix A).

after.justification: v2 retains the same original benchmark results, ablations, citation analyses and 20-participant user study, including the appendix results.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains identical paragraph/citation intent representations, inference procedures and implicit, explicit and multiview SFT variants. The appendix pre-planning and schema variants are also unchanged.

E1.justification: Both use the same SQA-CS-V2, DeepScholar Bench and ResearchQA evaluations, OpenScholar training queries and user-study population. No dataset, task, domain or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Default-generation and baseline-SFT comparisons are unchanged, as are the CoT and ReAct comparators in Table 5. Comparator membership remains identical throughout the main text and appendices.

E3.justification: The splits, sample sizes, retrieval controls, metrics, evaluation judges, model configurations and training settings are unchanged (Section 4.1 and Appendix A.1). The user-study procedures in Appendix A.9 also match.

E4.justification: Both retain identical intent-category ablations, pre-planning experiments, schema comparisons, citation-behavior analyses and user-study evidence. No supplementary analysis is added or revised.

E5.justification: Section 4.2 retains the paired t-tests with p-values 0.013 and 0.072 and alpha 0.1. The user-study uncertainty summaries and statistical procedures are unchanged; no run-count or seed information is added.

E6.justification: All numerical results and qualitative findings match, including Tables 2–10, Figure 2 and the appendix user-study results. For example, Table 2 reports Gemini overall scores of 88.1 without intents and 89.7 with intents in both versions.

T1.justification: The task formalization in Section 3.1 and subsequent definitions are identical. Neither version introduces additional theorems, proofs, assumptions or derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about intent-aware generation, distillation, attribution and readability, including the advertised average improvements of 2.9 and 12.3 absolute points.

C2.justification: Interpretations of citation gains and o3's citation behavior are unchanged. Both retain the same qualifications about synthetic intent schemas, hierarchical intents, domain generalization and schema consistency (Sections 4–5 and Appendix A.8).

D1.justification: The first-page code/data link changes from the GitHub repository colinzhaoust/intent-aware-deep-research to allenai/intent-aware-lfqa/tree/main. This updates access information; the PDFs do not establish changed resource contents or availability. Implementation details and prompts remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, cited works, bibliography and positioning relative to earlier research are identical.

P1.justification: The marginal arXiv identification text changes from v1 dated 28 March 2026 to v2 dated 7 August 2026. This is a limited metadata edit; the prose, terminology, headings and document structure remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The updated repository address changes first-page footnote spacing and wrapping, and the arXiv stamp's appearance changes. All figures, tables and the layouts of pages 2–39 remain visually identical.

improvement.justification: The revision updates a repository pointer and first-page presentation while leaving the scientific content, evidence, explanations and limitations unchanged. The PDFs do not establish improved or reduced resource availability, and the visible edits make no meaningful difference to overall paper quality.
